Subject: Pilot dataset conveyance & MAP proposed start

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. BrightWorks is ready to move to a short pilot with Redwood for inference benchmarking. We have a ~12k-row testcase pack and a small annotated prompt pack we can share for a 6-week evaluation.

Quick asks from our side before we transfer files:
- A mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and signoffs so procurement knows when to cut the PO.
- Usage constraints: We need to confirm the dataset remains in the pilot sandbox, no model training allowed, and a 90‑day retention window post-pilot.
- Evidence of audit logging and ability to revoke access at any time.

I attached a ZIP of the candidate testcases (BrightWorks_TestSuite_v1.zip) and a short readme. Can your team propose the MAP timeline and the token/scoping approach for ephemeral access?

Best,
Sam

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Sam —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample bundle. Confirmed we received BrightWorks_TestSuite_v1.zip and the readme. Draft MAP attached (Redwood_MAP_Template_v2.docx) with a proposed 6-week cadence and clear acceptance gates. High-level answers inline below.

Usage constraints (proposed):
- Environment: pilot assets ingested to an isolated sandbox (customer-tenant) under Redwood Dedicated pilot cluster. No cross-tenant sharing.
- Training: explicit prohibition on model weight updates or full-model fine-tuning — allowed: inference, reranking, and distilled evaluation only.
- Retention: default ingest retention = 90 days; export/take-down window 7 days after close.
- Revocation/Audit: Token-based ephemeral access tokens scoped to read-only inference; audit logs (per-request latency + token + route) retained 180 days and exportable as CSV.

Milestones (high-level):
1) Week 0 (Dec 6): Sign MAP + security questionnaire answered
2) Week 1 (Dec 8–12): Secure transfer + ingest to sandbox, smoke tests
3) Weeks 2–5: Evaluation run (performance + quality), weekly syncs
4) Week 6 (Jan 17): Acceptance window + final report + take-down

Would you like us to mark week 0 as Dec 6 for procurement to align PO? If yes, we can produce a fillable MAP spreadsheet for signature.

Attaching: Redwood_MAP_Template_v2.docx (edit-friendly) — please populate the owner columns and procurement info.

Thanks — looping in Lauren for acceptance criteria and Stephanie for security confirmation. PrIyom is on operational handoff if we need capacity tweaks.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Marcus / Sam —

Thanks for the draft. A couple of security items we need clarified before we sign:
- Can Redwood confirm that inference logs will exclude prompt content in the default export? We can agree to redacted logs but need request-level auditability.
- Do you support host-based encryption for the sandbox (we use customer-managed keys)?
- Are we allowed to run lightweight evaluation models that use KV cache but not persist model parameters?

I attached our security questionnaire with fields highlighted — please fill the sections under "data handling" and "key management." If we can get those answers by EOD Friday, procurement will aim for PO the following week.

Best,
Aisha Kapoor
Head of Legal & Compliance | BrightWorks
aisha.kapoor@brightworks.ai

From: lauren_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@brightworks.ai>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@brightworks.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot dataset conveyance & MAP proposed start

Hi Aisha / Sam —

Quick answers to the security points, happy to expand in a short call:

- Logs & redaction: By default we redact PII and prompt content from exportable audit trails. We keep full request traces in the control plane for 180 days for internal debugging; access is role-restricted and can be exported in a redacted CSV. If BrightWorks needs a stricter retention/redaction policy we can scope it in the MAP.

- Key management: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in the pilot. For the hosted pilot we can integrate your KMS via a key-wrapping flow — detail steps listed in the attached MAP template.

- Lightweight eval models: Allowed. We define allowed compute as non-persistent inference-only containers; KV-cache usage is fine so long as no checkpointing of model weights occurs. That meets your "no training" requirement.

Proposed acceptance criteria (short):
- Ingest successful and smoke test pass within 3 business days
- Baseline latency and throughput within 20% of demo numbers
- No seeding of training pipelines observed
- Final acceptance signoff by BrightWorks ML lead (Sam) and Legal (Aisha)

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7831) and our MAP folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3MAP).

If that looks good, Marcus — please generate the MAP spreadsheet (we'll attach DocuSign-ready copy).

—Lauren
